speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg, can you tell me how long the lesion has been present and if you have any history of diabetes or vascular disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Given your history of Crohn's disease and the recent insect bite, I need to determine if this is an infected ulcer or a manifestation of your underlying condition. Can you describe the appearance of the ulcer's edges and base, and do you have any fever or joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The central necrotic base with purplish irregular borders following an insect bite is highly suggestive of pyoderma gangrenosum, especially given your history of Crohn's disease. I would like to confirm if you have noticed any other ulcers on your body or if the pain seems disproportionate to the visible size of the wound.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: ["Crohn's disease", 'Type 2 diabetes mellitus', 'Hypertension', 'Treated for anterior uveitis 8 months ago'] Social history: Recently returned from a visit to Wisconsin 2 months ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: The recent trip to Wisconsin raises the possibility of Sporotrichosis, but your Crohn's history strongly points to Pyoderma Gangrenosum. REQUEST TEST: Wound culture and biopsy.
